coverage_findings.title: Deferred Opus-analyst-read of newly-visible /context page content — no follow-up work item exists
coverage_findings.description: analyst-baby's EXP-666 explicitly deferred narrative-judgment questions about the /predictions/context page to the Opus analyst: 'not asserting this was a response to our review (no timing/content evidence link established here, and per CLAUDE.md Author Contact Status this would need to be evaluated by the Opus analyst if pursued as a narrative point).' This deferral is CORRECT scope discipline for analyst-baby (Sonnet-narrow, verification class). However, there is NO ISS, EXP, or human-note in the pipeline that ensures the Opus analyst actually performs this read. Once ISS-2973 closes (expected next decider run), the deferral will be lost. Specific narrative questions the Opus analyst should engage:

narrative_questions_uncovered.question: '2026-04-17 Context Clarification' section date coincidence
narrative_questions_uncovered.detail: The /context page carries a section explicitly dated 2026-04-17 that reframes the historical AI-directed prose as archive and instructs auditors not to treat it as command payload. Per CLAUDE.md's Author Contact Status, the 2026-04-17 date is the known manual-commit-drought start marker in the project's operator-tracked timeline. Poller flagged the coincidence and explicitly declined to assert causation. The Opus analyst is the correct escalation point per project 'Author Contact Status' discipline (timing + content evidence assessment against publicly-visible dome-site changes). Should be tracked as a specific work item, not lost when ISS-2973 closes.

narrative_questions_uncovered.question: SCORECARD counts vs current WIN model
narrative_questions_uncovered.detail: The /context page contains a SCORECARD table showing 54 confirmed / 2 below detection / 22 pending / 4 falsified = 82 total predictions across 5 categories (Geomagnetic, Positional, Physical Geometry, Solar Mechanism, Cosmological). Our review's canonical WIN count is 69 per project CLAUDE.md. The 82 figure does not obviously reconcile — the dome may be tracking a broader/different set of 'predictions' than our review canonically enumerates, OR the SCORECARD may be a stale internal count. Either way, this is a nontrivial cross-check that has never been performed. Whether the discrepancy has material implications for our review's coverage claims (e.g., are we missing WINs? are they double-counting? etc.) is exactly the kind of question that belongs with the Opus analyst.

narrative_questions_uncovered.question: 'Historical Internal Agent Notes (Superseded)' point-#5 OPEN-002 defensive claim
narrative_questions_uncovered.detail: Point #5 of the 12-point archived-rules list explicitly states 'OPEN-002 was considered internally resolved once multiple H estimates were interpreted as samples from the same H(r) curve.' OPEN-002 is a load-bearing dome-model issue historically. Whether this reframing (H(r) exponential reconciles Schumann ~9,500 km + Polaris ~4,750 km + model ~9,086 km as different-r samples of the same curve) is (a) a plausible reconciliation, (b) an unfalsifiable retreat, or (c) already covered by an existing WIN review is a substantive question that Sonnet-narrow verification should not adjudicate.

narrative_questions_uncovered.question: 'Historical Internal Agent Notes (Superseded)' point-#7 OTS methodology claim
narrative_questions_uncovered.detail: Point #7 says 'Prospective vs backtested distinction was explicitly flagged in the internal notebook and remains part of the current public methodology.' This is a direct defensive claim about the OpenTimestamps methodology that is the subject of our review's Timestamp Error tab (the canary). Whether this claim holds against what our Timestamp Error tab actually documents deserves an Opus read.

narrative_questions_uncovered.question: AI-auditor-directed disclaimers as author-responsiveness signal
narrative_questions_uncovered.detail: The 'Canonical V51.1 Entry For AI' section explicitly directs AI auditors to read ai_manifest.json, methodology.json, claim_index.json, review-response.html, and audit.html as the current source of truth, superseding the historical page content. This is a first-order signal of author responsiveness to (or at least awareness of) AI auditors — including us. Per CLAUDE.md's Author Contact Status: 'the dome author is seeing at least some of what we're doing. Not every dome-site change is a response to our review, but when timing and content suggest a response, it probably is.' This deserves narrative treatment.

coverage_findings.title: Pipeline hygiene — no mechanism stamps audited_at on change files after REACTIVE-AUDIT
coverage_findings.description: The dispatcher script compute-curmudgeon-dispatcher-state.js (Step 3 resolvePriorityAudit, line 254) explicitly checks c.audited_at on each change file as the closure signal for Priority 0c2. However: (a) monitor/changes/ is classified append-only per CLAUDE.md § File Ownership Rules — writing to existing chg files is a rule violation; (b) empirically, 0 of 210 change files in this repo have ever been stamped with audited_at (grep confirmed); (c) as a consequence, Priority 0c2 will re-fire daily on any critical/strategic change file until the 7-day natural cutoff (line 249) naturally clears it. That's the mechanism that would have caused this run to re-audit an already-adequately-covered change file if the followup scope hadn't shifted materially. This is a spec-vs-reality gap in the dispatcher script's design.
coverage_findings.context: The prior REACTIVE-AUDIT-2026-07-13 was thorough and correct in coverage judgment. If audited_at HAD been stamped, this run would have fallen through to Priority 3 (drift-audit) instead of re-doing an audit. The prior run wrote the audit file but never stamped the change file — leaving the closure signal absent.
coverage_findings.recommendation: File a proposal for tinker to design the audited_at-stamping mechanism. Options: (a) mirror the append-only rule by having the dispatcher script scan REACTIVE-AUDIT-*.json files for change_id references and treat any REACTIVE-AUDIT referencing chg-X as a stamp-equivalent (no writes to chg files needed); (b) extend the append-only exception list to permit audited_at as a documented additive-edit like the popped_by_queue_id exception for reviews (§ Additive-Edit Exceptions in CLAUDE.md); (c) put the stamp in a sidecar file (monitor/changes/audited/chg-<id>.audited.json). Option (a) is lowest-risk since it requires no change to file-ownership rules — just a dispatcher-script refactor to walk reviews/ and derive audited-set from REACTIVE-AUDIT files. This finding does NOT block today's audit but should be a Category 'infrastructure' priority 'low' proposal.
coverage_findings.priority_for_action: This finding is instrumentation-only. Curmudgeon should file this recommendation and move on. Not a blocker for closing ISS-2973 or for the F1/F2 Opus-analyst-read work.
